items.title: Kenny Barron — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I got to hear Coleman Hawkins and people like that, Ben Webster. For me, that was really great.

ctx.x: Touring. What were your recollections of touring?

One thing that was nice with Dizzy: we were guaranteed to work 40 weeks out of the year. That was guaranteed. It was a lot easier during those times, because most of the clubs you worked at, you were there for two, sometimes three weeks. We would start out – Birdland, for instance. We were always there for two weeks. Then we would go to Chicago. We’d work the London House for three weeks. Go out on the West Coast. Do the Jazz Workshop for three weeks. Go down to the Lighthouse for three weeks. Those kind of…
The band was pretty cohesive, not that many personnel changes in Dizzy’s group.
